description: Passages where whole sections of the Bible run in parallel: the synoptic Gospels and the parts of John that tell the same events, Samuel and Kings with Chronicles, Kings with Isaiah 36-39 and Jeremiah 52, the Psalms reproduced in the histories and repeated in the Psalter, the genealogies of Chronicles with Genesis, Ruth and Joshua, Ezra 2 with Nehemiah 7, and the Ten Commandments in Exodus and Deuteronomy. Verses are OSIS ids (Matt.12.29), a range is "Matt.12.22-Matt.12.30", and a member of several pieces is a list; the numbering is English (the KJV and ESV). A row pairs a main passage with a parallel. The main passage is the first book canonically (in the Gospels Matthew, then Mark, then Luke, then John; where Matthew has nothing the first of the others), except that Psalms is always the main passage of a Psalm reproduced elsewhere. A passage in several books is one row per pair. "match" says how the verses go together: "each" matches the verses of the two passages one by one, in order, and they are the same length; "all" matches each verse of one with every verse of the other, for where the books drift apart or tell the same thing differently. Every row was aligned verse by verse against the KJV text.
